## Evidence re-gathered first-hand before changing anything, and it REJECTS this ticket's own framing

I was asked to hold every alarm change to a falsifiable-hypothesis bar rather than act on inherited
leads. Doing that changed one of my conclusions, so recording the measurement here.

**8-hour `get-metric-statistics` sweep, 2026-09-05 11:27Z-19:27Z**, `period=300`, 96 buckets per
metric — wide enough that absence is meaningful. (Timestamps come back with a `-07:00` offset and
the namespace is lowercase `rebar/host`; both produce a false "no data" if got wrong.)

| observability.sh line | metric | present | max gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 112 `GerritReachable` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 161 `mcp_healthy` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 169 `disk_used_percent` (/var/gerrit) | | 93% | 10 min |
| 192 `root_disk_used_percent` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 213 `gate_scratch_mounted` | | 93% | 10 min |
| 601 `docker_storage_used_percent` | | 70% | 35 min |
| 622/640 `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` / `docker_unaccounted_bytes` | | 31% | 60 min |
| 696/713/771 `journal_cap_in_effect` / `journal_used_percent` / `var_tmp_cleanup_active` | | 69% | 40 min |
| 798 `var_tmp_used_percent` | | **0%** | — |
| 940 `data_disk_debris_bytes` | | 56% | 60 min |
| 1193-1301 the S5/S4b/88ab/autodeploy counters | | 48-53% | 60-70 min |
| 1463/1511 `g2p_dispatch_errors` / `mirror_out_of_sync` | | 43% | **85 min** |

### The discriminating result

This ticket's description attributes the empty buckets to **cadence aliasing** — a publisher whose
interval drifts against fixed 5-minute buckets. That hypothesis predicts a **FLAT** presence profile
across metrics, because every metric rides the same run. **It is not flat.** Presence declines
monotonically with position in the script, 93% at line 213 to 43% at line 1511, and the two large
off-trend dips are exactly the metrics published only on a SUCCESSFUL `du`.

So the description's mechanism is wrong, and `ignitable-fuchsia-kawala` (`9313-1fac-9f32-4b07`) is
right: the probe is SIGTERM-ed mid-run. The measured "13% of buckets empty" in the description was
taken on a head-of-script metric and does not describe the tail, which is 31-56%. My own initial
framing ("5-9 minute contractual inter-arrival") inherited the same error and is corrected in the
change.

What survives unchanged is the **alarm-side** half of the defect, which is independent of why the
gaps exist: `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` with `datapoints_to_alarm < evaluation_periods` lets
missing buckets out-vote a real datapoint. That is what makes an ordinary gap page and what makes a
fired alarm unclearable.

### Evidence class per alarm, from datapoints not StateReason

**(b) publishes, value does not breach — alarm is WRONG (15):** `deploy_errors`, `mcp_mem_abort`,
`mcp_retire_cap`, `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded`, `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable`,
`g2p_dispatch_errors`, `replication_errors`, `review_bot_merge_change_errors`, `mirror_out_of_sync`,
`data_disk_debris_bytes` — all `min=max=0` across 8 h; `journal_used_percent` 57 vs 85;
`journal_cap_in_effect` constant 1 vs `<1`; `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` max 10 vs 85;
`docker_storage_used_percent` max 46 vs 85; `voter_errors` 0 at the firing time. `mirror_out_of_sync`
also confirmed out-of-band: Gerrit and GitHub `main` agree at `4c9940348148`.

**(a) genuinely breaching — alarm is CORRECT, untouched in threshold (2):** `gate_scratch_mounted`
= 0 (93% present) and `var_tmp_cleanup_active` = 0 (69% present). Both keep firing under the new
window, proven rather than assumed: every published datapoint in 8 h is breaching, so every period
in a 6-period window breaches.

**(a) but the METRIC is defective (1):** `docker_unaccounted_bytes` genuinely read 2.31 GB against a
2 GiB bound at 10:12 PDT — but its StateReason is "1 datapoint was received for 3 periods and 2
missing datapoints were treated as [Breaching]", so the ALARM state was still reached on gaps, and
`regretful-enormous-horsefly` establishes ~56% of the value is xfs block overhead. Threshold not
touched; a revert condition is recorded because `M = N` deliberately waits for a persistent crossing
on what is a rising trend metric.

**(c) no data at all (2):** `gate_scratch_disk_high` and `var_tmp_used_percent` — **zero datapoints
in 8 hours**. These are data-availability defects; the upstream causes are `dcc3` (unmounted volume)
and the pending `rootflags=pquota` reboot. Retuning their thresholds would be a no-op dressed as a
fix, so nothing of the sort was done: they stay RED under the new tuning because an entirely empty
window still satisfies `M = N` on a breaching alarm. What changes is only that they can CLEAR when
data returns.

### Independent corroboration of the real firings, and one against my own change

`voter_errors` recorded SIX non-zero datapoints in the window — 1, 1, 1, 9 at 05:17-05:32 PDT and
1, 2 at 08:37-08:42. The first cluster is three consecutive breaching datapoints, so it satisfies
`datapoints_to_alarm = 3` under the NEW 3-of-6 notBreaching shape as well as the old 3-of-5. That is
detection preserved against a real historical event rather than against an argument. The second
cluster is two datapoints and fires under neither shape, old or new — also unchanged.

### What is NOT proven, stated as such

`rebar-gerrit-gate-down`, `rebar-mcp-serving-path-down` and `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` are all
currently **OK**. I widened their windows anyway on the ground that their measured max gap is
exactly 10.0 min against a 10-minute window, i.e. one bucket alignment from a false page. That is
hardening on a near-miss, not a proven false firing, and it is labelled that way.

No threshold, unit, metric or period is changed by this ticket. Terraform is written and validated
(`fmt -check` and `validate` both clean); it is NOT applied. Full derivation, per-alarm dispositions,
detection proofs and five revert conditions are in `infra/runbooks/alarm-window-tuning.md`; the
invariants are enforced offline by `tests/unit/test_alarm_window_tuning.py`.
